name: Historic Walled Town of Cuenca
description: Cuenca is a medieval walled town in Castilla–La Mancha, Spain, perched on a narrow ridge between the Júcar and Huécar river gorges. Built as a Moorish fortress and taken by Castile in 1177, it is known for its casas colgadas, or hanging houses, which cling to the edge of sheer cliffs. It also has Spain's first Gothic cathedral.
